items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Ori had a brass band. Black Benny was playing bass drum with him.

ctx.x: Ori had a brass band. Black Benny was playing bass drum with him. I can't remember all the players. He was with him. He had a little brass band. Mm-hmm.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Him and Red Happy and Black Benny and a few more of them, you know. Just jive singing.

ctx.x: Did he sing when he was young?

No, at that time, you know, he jived around. Some of him and the boys around, they walked around for D.A. Liberty, little quartets. Him and Red Happy and Black Benny and a few more of them, you know. Just jive singing. Kids, you know, like they were doing the street jazz.
Where was Nick of Themis from here, my band?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: Black Benny played first, until he got killed, and Henry Martin played until the band broke up.

ctx.x: Did you play snare or bass drum? Snare. Snare. Snare. Henry Martin played bass drum.
Henry Martin. Black Benny played first, until he got killed, and Henry Martin played until the band broke up.

How was Manuel Perez? Some people talk like he was the greatest of ever, and others say that he wasn't such a hot trumpet player, just a note reader, and that he really couldn't think anything. How did you like him? What did he sound like? He was a legitimate trumpet player.
